issues.legal_issue: A conviction for attempted murder may be sustained where the accused’s intention to kill is established from the circumstances and the accused committed an overt act in execution of that intention, even if the victim’s injuries were not independently proved through every available medical record.
material_facts: The accused struck the victim on the head with a pharsi.
The victim became unconscious and deeply comatose and had a large extradural haematoma that required urgent surgery.
A neurosurgeon testified that without the operation the head injury would have caused the victim’s death.
Two injured eyewitnesses described the assault, and their evidence was corroborated by medical evidence.
The victim did not testify, and the defence relied on the absence of certain scan, X-ray and operation records.
issues.conclusion: The conviction for attempted murder was upheld because the weapon, the head injury, the severity of the blows and the medical evidence supported the finding of an intention to kill and an overt act in execution of that intention.
issues.legal_principle: Section 307 IPC requires proof of an intention to commit murder and an act done in furtherance of that intention; a fatal or otherwise death-capable injury is not essential. Intention may be inferred from circumstances including the weapon used, the part of the body targeted and the nature and severity of the injuries. The Court relied on State of M.P. v. Kashiram, State of Maharashtra v. Balram Bama Patil, Girija Shanker v. State of U.P., R. Prakash v. State of Karnataka and State of M.P. v. Saleem. It also held that injured eyewitnesses’ evidence is entitled to great weight and requires cogent and convincing grounds to discard when it is credible and medically corroborated.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and accused_used_dangerous_weapon_on_vital_body_part and victim_sustained_severe_head_injury and medical_evidence_supports_seriousness and injured_witnesses_give_credible_corroborated_account

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The matter is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.accused_used_dangerous_weapon_on_vital_b: The accused used a dangerous weapon to strike a vital part of the victim’s body.
predicates.victim_sustained_severe_head_injury: The victim sustained a severe head injury.
predicates.medical_evidence_supports_seriousness: Medical evidence supports the seriousness of the victim’s injury and the treatment it required.
predicates.injured_witnesses_give_credible_corrobor: Witnesses injured in the incident gave a credible account of the assault that was corroborated by medical evidence.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns an assault in which a dangerous weapon was used on a vital body part, the resulting head injury was severe, medical evidence supports its seriousness, and injured witnesses give a credible corroborated account, the attempted-murder conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: The custodial sentences of offenders convicted of causing injuries may be reduced to the period already served in light of the circumstances of the offence and the time already spent in custody.
material_facts: The offenders inflicted injuries with a jaily and lathis during the incident.
Their convictions for causing injuries were confirmed on appeal.
The incident arose from a dispute over cutting reeds and a wordy altercation.
The occurrence had taken place many years before the appeal was decided, and the offenders had already served periods in custody.
issues.conclusion: The convictions were confirmed, but the custodial sentences were reduced to the periods already undergone by the respective offenders.
issues.legal_principle: Sentencing is discretionary and must account for the gravity and nature of the offence, the motive, the manner of its commission and other attendant circumstances. The Court relied on State of M.P. v. Bablu Natt, Alister Anthony Pareira v. State of Maharashtra and Soman v. State of Kerala.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and injury_offenders_have_confirmed_convictions and assault_arose_from_dispute_and_altercation and substantial_time_has_elapsed and offenders_already_served_custody

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The matter is an appeal challenging criminal convictions and sentences.
predicates.injury_offenders_have_confirmed_convicti: The offenders’ convictions for causing injuries have been confirmed.
predicates.assault_arose_from_dispute_and_altercati: The assault arose from a dispute followed by a wordy altercation.
predicates.substantial_time_has_elapsed: A substantial period passed between the offence and the appellate decision.
predicates.offenders_already_served_custody: The offenders had already served periods in custody.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns confirmed convictions for injuries caused in an assault arising from a dispute and altercation, substantial time has passed, and the offenders have served custody, their custodial sentences may be reduced to the time already served.

issues.legal_issue: A sentence for attempted murder may be reduced to the period already served while compensation is ordered for a victim who suffered serious injuries and trauma.
material_facts: The offender had been in custody for more than three years when the sentence was reconsidered.
The assault arose during a dispute over reeds and a wordy altercation.
The victim suffered grievous head injuries, was deeply comatose, underwent urgent surgery and experienced treatment-related trauma.
The offender had offered compensation, but the victim had refused that offer.
issues.conclusion: The custodial sentence was reduced to the period already served, and the offender was ordered to pay compensation to the victim, with a further custodial sentence to apply in default of payment.
issues.legal_principle: The court must exercise sentencing discretion by considering the gravity of the offence, the motive, the nature of the offence and all attendant circumstances. Section 357(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure permits an order for compensation. The Court relied on Hari Singh v. Sukhbir Singh for compensation and on State of M.P. v. Bablu Natt, Alister Anthony Pareira v. State of Maharashtra and Soman v. State of Kerala for sentencing discretion.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_attempted_murder: The matter is an appeal challenging a sentence for attempted murder.
predicates.offender_has_served_substantial_custody: The offender has already served a substantial period in custody.
predicates.assault_arose_from_dispute_and_altercati: The assault arose from a dispute followed by a wordy altercation.
predicates.victim_sustained_grievous_injuries_and_t: The victim suffered grievous injuries and trauma, including serious consequences requiring treatment.

issues.definition: When an attempted-murder sentence is appealed after the offender has served substantial custody, the assault arose from a dispute and altercation, and the victim suffered grievous injuries and trauma, the custodial sentence may be reduced to time already served and compensation ordered.
